citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care.
citations.narrative:
On August 11, 2026, female pig #9727, housed in pen #9 of the Ponderosa East building with two other female pigs, was
observed with extensive superficial skin lesions. These lesions included numerous linear and irregular reddish brown
scratches across multiple body regions. Several areas exhibited dark brown to reddish crusts and scabs consistent with
partially healed wounds. Affected areas included the face, shoulders, back, and hindquarters. In addition, regions of red,
inflamed skin and residual scarring were present. The animal caretaker reported noticing a few scratches the previous
morning. However, the progression to more severe, widespread lesions was observed on the morning of August 11, 2026.
These findings were not reported to test facility management as required by the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for
Routine Animal Health, Morbidity, and Mortality. Failure to observe and report wounds in a timely manner can result in
delayed medical assessment and intervention. This may contribute to increased inflammation, pain, risk of infection, and
further injuries sustained from interactions with other pigs within the enclosure. Each research facility shall establish and
maintain programs of adequate veterinary care that include daily observations of all animals to assess their health and
well-being. A mechanism of direct and frequent communication is required so that timely and accurate information on
problems of animal health, behavior, and well-being is conveyed to the attending veterinarian. This was corrected at the
time of inspection by moving the pig to an isolated pen and notifying the attending veterinarian.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the attending veterinarian and the IACUC chair.
